title: Why and How to Do Science When AI Is Better at It: A Framework Grounded in Human Understanding and Direction
abstract: arXiv:2610.36116v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As AI begins to match or exceed human researchers at core scientific tasks, two questions become pressing: \emph{why} should humans keep doing science, and \emph{how} should they use AI when they do? This paper argues that the second can be answered only by answering the first. It holds that one indispensable aim of science is \emph{durable, collective human understanding of the world, pursued in service of human ends and values}. From this principle it derives a two-part test for when a research task can be delegated to AI. The first part, \emph{human understanding}, requires that the scientific community remain able to explain, defend and contest the resulting claims, and retain the skills to do so. The second, \emph{human direction}, requires that judgments about which questions matter and what findings mean stay with accountable humans. translated_title: 当AI更擅长科学时，为何以及如何做科学：一个基于人类理解与人类主导的框架
translated_abstract: 随着AI开始在核心科学任务上达到甚至超越人类研究者的水平，两个问题变得日益紧迫：人类为什么应该继续做科学，以及在做科学时应该如何使用AI？本文认为，只有回答了第一个问题，才能回答第二个问题。本文主张，科学的一个不可或缺的目标是“对世界的持久、集体性的人类理解，并以人类的目的和价值观为依归”。基于这一原则，本文推导出一个两部分的检验标准，用以判断何时可以将研究任务委托给AI。第一部分是“人类理解”，要求科学界仍然能够解释、捍卫和质疑由此产生的科学主张，并保留这样做所需的技能。第二部分是“人类主导”，要求关于哪些问题重要以及研究发现意味着什么的判断由负责任的人类来掌握。将该检验标准应用于贡献者角色分类法（CRediT）中研究的各个阶段，得出了相应建议。
tldr: 本文提出“人类理解”与“人类主导”两部分检验标准，论证科学的核心目标是服务于人类目的与价值观的持久集体理解，并据此判断哪些研究任务可以委托给AI、哪些必须保留在负责任的人类手中。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that science's indispensable aim is durable, collective human understanding in service of human ends and values, and derives a two-part test—human understanding and human direction—for deciding when research tasks can be delegated to AI.
